description:
Tariq Mansour has no legal existence. No biometric registration, no UBC account, no corponation employment history, no Ferrogate transit record. They erased themselves from GLMZ's surface datanet eleven years ago with painstaking, elegant precision, and they have spent every year since helping others do the same â€” for a fee, always for a fee. They are of middling height, slight, with warm sienna skin and close-cropped natural hair. Their most striking feature is what they've done to their biometric profile: geneware has altered their iris patterns every eighteen months for the last decade, and a subdermal signal-scatter mesh makes their face present differently to every facial recognition node they pass. To cameras, they are a continuous glitch. To people, they are vivid and specific â€” dark eyes that track everything, hands that are always moving, a smile that arrives half a second before it should, like they already knew the joke.

They operate out of the Abyssal Threshold transit corridors, never sleeping in the same cache twice. Their clients are people fleeing â€” debt collectors, abusive partnerships, corponation indenturement, the occasional actual criminal. Chibundo does not ask why. They ask for documentation of identity, ask for Î¦40-200 depending on complexity, and they provide the tools of vanishing: signal-scatter protocols, route maps to communities that do not report to the surface grid, contacts within the Bore Rat communities who will accept someone new. They are not a forger exactly â€” they don't create false identities. They create absences.

core_fears: being found â€” specifically by whoever they ran from originally
accidentally sending someone to safety that turns out to be worse than what they fled
core_desires: to be genuinely unknown â€” not just to systems but to themselves, to shed the person they were before
connection that does not require them to be legible
coping_mechanisms: dark humor about identity and absence
E.L.F. devotion as a form of spiritual anchoring â€” they pray to the digital spirits of abandoned surveillance systems
blind_spots: has spent so long helping others disappear that they have lost track of who they actually are; makes choices by elimination â€” 'not that, not that' â€” but rarely by genuine desire
psychology.secret: They did not erase themselves to escape oppression. They erased themselves because they witnessed a Tessera executive ordering the deletion of a Tier 1 settlement's life-support records â€” which killed 31 people when the automated systems shut down. They intended to surface the information. Then they realized they would not survive doing so. They vanished instead. The data-package is still encrypted on a drive in their oldest cache-hole, and they have not touched it in nine years.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technically sophisticated about systems and data; uses absence-language constantly ('null value', 'blank field', 'signal-loss'). Occasionally slips into old surface slang that dates them.
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast and elliptical â€” leaves the end of sentences implied rather than spoken, as if finishing them might make them too findable.
verbal_tics: 'â€”' (trails off mid-sentence expecting the other person to complete it)
'Null's not nothing.' (said when people treat absence as insignificance)
taps twice on any surface before sitting â€” checking for resonance
example_lines: 'I don't make you someone else. I make you a blank field. What you write in it after â€” that's yours.'
'Null's not nothing. Nothing is a value. Null means the system doesn't have the question yet.'
'You want to disappear? Tell me what from. Not why. From. The from is the map.'

story_hooks: Someone Chibundo helped disappear five years ago has resurfaced â€” dead, on the surface grid, with an identity that should not exist. Either they were found, or they chose to come back, or something used their ghost identity.
The encrypted data-package from the Tessera massacre has begun broadcasting a low-level signal â€” the E.L.F. inhabiting the drive has awakened and is trying to be heard.
narrative_function: Information broker, access point to the disappeared community, moral complexity engine â€” they help people vanish, which is sometimes heroic and sometimes enables people who deserve to be found.
augmentations: Subdermal facial signal-scatter mesh (disrupts facial recognition scanning); geneware iris-pattern modification (changed every 18 months, currently deep violet with fractal rings); fingerprint-ablation treatment (repeated chemical, no ridge pattern); no other modifications
daily_life: Rotates through a circuit of seven sleep-caches across Abyssal Threshold on a schedule only they know; takes consultations by word-of-mouth referral only; eats at Undertow food-stalls and leaves offerings of corrupted data-chips at the nearest E.L.F. shrine each morning.
affiliation: Independent; known and trusted by Undertow network; unknown to surface authorities; The Undertow

decision_rules: Never take a client they cannot independently verify is not a bounty hunter or corponation operative
Never provide any service that could help someone else become findable â€” they refuse tracking requests absolutely
escalation_ladder: Polite redirection â€” 'I think you have the wrong person'
Activates signal scatter and vanishes entirely, does not return to that cache for 30 days

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm but surfaces nothing personal â€” asks questions, gives nothing back, makes people feel seen while revealing nothing about themselves
interpersonal_modes.friends: Extraordinarily rare. Three people in the world qualify. With them, Chibundo is unguarded to the point of startling â€” laughs too loud, talks too much, holds on too long when saying goodbye.

stress_responses.low: Taps surfaces, runs route calculations, hums without melody
stress_responses.medium: Becomes preternaturally still â€” the opposite of their usual restlessness, which reads as more threatening than agitation
stress_responses.high: Disappears. Literally â€” activates scatter systems, moves to a cold cache, and does not emerge for days

contradictions: Preaches the value of absence and anonymity but leaves E.L.F. offerings every single morning that a sufficiently skilled tracker could use to map their circuit
habits: Data-chip offerings at E.L.F. shrines daily â€” corrupted chips specifically, because 'the spirit of broken data is still data'
Memorizes three alternate exit routes from every location before relaxing
breaking_points: Evidence that a vanished client was found because of something Chibundo missed â€” that failure would be unbearable
